name: manual_de193e
claim: When supervising child processes via HTTP loopback proxies under spend bounds, enforce five structural patterns: (1) Synchronous socket admission in process_request before spawning handler threads; (2) Three-phase lifecycle (RUNNING -> DRAINING -> CLOSED) where stop_and_drain sets _accepting=False, calls server.shutdown() explicitly, awaits the condition-variable drain of active handlers, and marks CLOSED on timeout to fence chat_gate dispatch; (3) Single fail-closed funnel in _fail_closed and _read_upstream_response: every transport and read error, including HTTPError.read timeouts, routes into the funnel, which classifies outcomes as ACCOUNTED, REJECTED (DEFINITIVE_REJECTIONS), or UNACCOUNTED (debited in full) and terminates fail-closed with exit 124; (4) Pre-forward provider-side budget clamping of max_tokens and max_completion_tokens; (5) Per-launch random session token authentication. On distributed task queues, preserve task_claims.claimed_at fencing tokens made strictly increasing via persistent task_claim_hwm table and nextafter(), requiring --expected-claimed-at or --unverified-legacy on worker CLI.

decisions.notes: Supersedes lesson_5c3598dee3cf (append-only; original rows retained). Review of PR 525 found the replacement dropped two steps from lesson_f7c090a572fc: the explicit server.shutdown() call plus condition-variable drain wait in stop_and_drain, and the rule that every transport and read error, including HTTPError.read timeouts, enters the fail-closed funnel and exits 124. This record restores both while keeping the three-phase RUNNING/DRAINING/CLOSED lifecycle with CLOSED on timeout and the high-water-mark claim fence.
